create.name: Ayya Sudhamma
create.bio:
Ayya Sudhamma is a Theravada Buddhist nun and the abbess of the Charlotte Buddhist Vihara, a small monastic residence in north-east Charlotte, the city where she was born in 1963. Before taking robes she trained in law at New York University and worked as an attorney in San Francisco. She left lay life in 1998, took novice vows the following year under Bhante Henepola Gunaratana at the Bhavana Society in West Virginia, and in 2003 received full bhikkhuni ordination in Sri Lanka, among the first American-born women to do so in the Theravada tradition. She then spent more than eight years as resident teacher at the Carolina Buddhist Vihara, a monastery in Greenville, South Carolina, and a year at Santi Forest Monastery in Australia, before returning home in 2013 to found the Charlotte vihara.

Her teaching stays close to the early Pali scriptures while speaking plainly to modern life: breath meditation, contemplation of the body, lovingkindness, karma and impermanence, and the verses of the first Buddhist nuns in the Therigatha. Several times a week she leads sittings and talks at the vihara, most of them also on Zoom, with sessions for beginners, a monthly half-day retreat in east Charlotte and traditional full-moon and festival observances. She helped found the North American Bhikkhuni Association and was honoured at the United Nations in Bangkok in 2006 as an outstanding woman in Buddhism.

courses.title: Meditate with the Monk: weekly meditation and Buddhist teaching
courses.description: Guided sittings and talks led by Ayya Sudhamma at the vihara in north-east Charlotte, several times a week, most of them also open on Zoom. Saturday sessions add a longer period of teaching and discussion, with the first Saturday of each month set aside for beginners.

free_resources.title: Guided Mindfulness of Breathing Meditation
free_resources.description: A twenty-minute guided sitting on the breath, recorded at the vihara, taking the listener step by step through settling and following each in-breath and out-breath.

free_resources.title: Short Meditation with Venerable Bhikkhunī Ayyā Sudhamma Mahātherī
free_resources.description: A brief guided practice of about six minutes, suitable for a pause in the day or as a first taste of sitting with her guidance.

free_resources.title: Aspects of the Eightfold Path (audio talk)
free_resources.description: A recorded dharma talk she gave to a Charlotte insight meditation group, walking through the strands of the Buddha's Eightfold Path and how they support one another in practice.

sprint.tier_evidence: Charlotte Buddhist Vihara YouTube channel 212 subscribers (channel header, 3 Nov 2026) is the vihara's shared account, not counted; Meetup group 2,474 members (group page, 3 Nov 2026) is a group, not counted; Facebook page is the vihara's and was not fetched; no personal accounts found → 0 own → local_hero
flags: Photo is from the vihara's Residents page, which describes only her; it shows a bhikkhuni in meditation and no other photo was found to cross-check, so identity is very likely but not independently confirmed.
No published email: the vihara's contact form is used. Its contact page also points people to the Meetup group for meeting details.

YouTube channel and Facebook page belong to the Charlotte Buddhist Vihara (her monastery), not to her personally; the channel is linked as youtube_url because nearly all its talks are hers, but its subscribers are not counted toward tier.
The vihara's robots.txt sets crawl-delay 60; requests were spaced at least 61 seconds apart.
Hub is her own monastery (not a Spiritpedia listing); teaches_at left empty.
Two videos are shared with Ayya Suvijjana (one kept, 'The Five Spiritual Faculties'); a third, 'The Path to Happiness with Ayya Suvijjana', is not hers and was left out.
Base and biography details (birth year, law career, ordination dates) come from the vihara's Residents page and her English Wikipedia article.
The Meetup group's 'About' text mentions meditation for stress reduction; that framing is not used in the plan.
left_out: Chants ('Nuns words for the Buddha chanted in Pali and English', Pali chant recordings): devotional chanting rather than teaching.
'MN 131' (95-minute sutta study with no description) and older lower-view talks: the twelve-video limit was reached with clearer titles.
'Ayya Sudhamma Audio Only Talk on The Aspects of the Eight Fold Path' on YouTube: the same talk is offered as an audio download from the vihara and listed once as a free resource.
Monthly morning retreat at Great Woods Zen and full-moon observances: no page of their own (only mentioned on Meetup).
Dharma Seed talks: not opened (no robots check made), so not added.
